_note: Official notices copied by hand from park websites (floridastateparks.org is Cloudflare-blocked to scripts). kind=closure rows make getParkStatus() return 'closed' while active and within starts_at/ends_at; deactivating a row (active=false) or setting ends_at in the past reopens the park automatically. severity uses the NWS scale: Severe (closure), Moderate, Minor. Verified 2026-09-18/19; the eight parks added later were checked against their official 'Know before you go' notices on 2026-09-19.

alerts.text: Effective Oct. 29, 2025: Due to construction renovations, there are no water activities available at Ruth B. Kirby Gilchrist Blue Springs State Park. The large pavilion, large picnic area and volleyball courts are open; port-o-let facilities are in place until renovations are complete. Rentals and concession services are also unavailable. No reopening date has been announced.

Effective Thursday, July 16, 2026: The designated swimming area at Poe Springs Park is temporarily closed due to poor water clarity, and is reassessed weekly. The rest of the park (picnic areas, trails, boat launch and paddling) remains open. In August 2026 the Florida Springs Institute reported that the spring had stopped flowing during drought; no reopening timeline has been given.

Effective March 17, 2026: The Midpoint Tube Launch is closed until further notice for repairs. Tubers can continue to launch from Dampier's Landing at the South Entrance until 5 p.m. Tube rentals end at 4:30 p.m.

Effective May 20, 2026: Expect high visitation on weekends and holidays. When the park reaches capacity it temporarily closes to all visitors, including those with rental reservations or digital day passes. Entry is first-come, first-served; visitors may not park and wait on the roadside, and local law enforcement will issue citations.

Effective Sept. 9, 2026: The parking lot at Rainbow Springs State Park will undergo renovations from Sept. 9, 2026 to Feb. 4, 2027. Limited parking will be available; the park may reach capacity earlier than usual.

Effective Sept. 2, 2025: Reservations are required for day-use entry to Wekiwa Springs State Park for all visitors, including annual passholders. Reservations open 60 days ahead; same-day reservations are available until the daily limit is met.

Park capacity information: Madison Blue Spring State Park experiences frequent closures between 10 a.m. and 3 p.m. on weekends and holidays due to high visitation. The park closes when it reaches capacity but may reopen to additional visitors later that day. For their safety, visitors are not permitted to park and wait in their cars on the side of the road or in the park entrance area; local law enforcement will issue citations.
Effective April 2, 2026: Large RVs, RVs pulling trailers or truck and camper combinations are not recommended at Madison Blue Spring State Park due to limited turnaround space.

Effective Aug. 20, 2026: The floating dock at Fanning Springs State Park will be undergoing an improvement project. Until further notice, swimming and boating will remain open but be prepared to be asked to exit at all times for safety purposes.

Effective Jan. 14, 2026: The waterfront restroom and dump station at Manatee Springs State Park are currently closed. There is no electric vehicle charging allowed in the park. ADA restrooms and showers remain open in the Magnolia 1 and Hickory camping loops.

Effective Dec. 12, 2025: Due to low water levels, the Wilderness River Cruise at Weeki Wachee Springs State Park is paused during daytime hours. The mermaid shows, Ranger Experience and Buccaneer Bay beach and swimming are unaffected.

Buccaneer Bay schedule: the beach and swimming are open daily, but the water slides and lazy river run on Saturdays and Sundays only from Aug. 11 to Sept. 27, 2026 and are closed for the season beginning Sept. 28, 2026. The kiddie pool is closed for renovations. Once the park is full, no more tickets are sold and you cannot re-enter.

Park capacity: each morning 280 vehicles are allowed into Kelly Park, and an additional 50 vehicles are admitted after 1 p.m. with an afternoon parking pass - about 330 vehicles and an average of 1,350 visitors a day. On a typical summer day the park fills within an hour of opening. You must collect a pass in the morning when the park first hits capacity to get in at the 1 p.m. re-opening (one pass per car, first-come, first-served). The county web page and the information line, 407-254-1906, are updated when the park is full.
